did: HOST4 (#3525): every emotion of Mochi, the owner's character, now has a loop. That covers the nine shared emotions and Mochi's own five beats (question, confusion, issue, intuition, hesitation), and the NFL celebration has one too: crouch, leap with arms up in a V, land, spike and dance, settling back to its start before it repeats. Each emotion is a typed pose, a pure function of the time since its beat's run began, drawn on new named parts of the cast's mochi. Every added part is drawn clear, so the still mochi is unchanged, and a test pins that. Byte snapshots pin every loop at three moments. The work sits on HOST3's helpers in host-draw.ts. Two fresh-context reviews and a line-justification pass found clipping at the box edge, a jump where the celebration loops, glints snapping, and a spiked ball tilting with the dance; all four were fixed. The owner saw the contact sheet (https://claude.ai/artifact/MSrqducsGrJr4zFJzMXbc5) and said: "I like them all ... that's green light for me."

calls.title: How Mochi shows each emotion (C1529)
options: Face and squash only: brows, eyes and mouth, no signs over the head
Face, squash and a sign per emotion, the signs clear until a loop shows them
A separate mochi drawing per emotion, swapped whole
calls.why: A sign per beat (a question mark, a swirl, a bang, a bulb, three dots) is what makes Mochi's own beats read in a long shot, and drawing every sign clear keeps the still mochi the same picture.
calls.undo: Drop a sign from that emotion's pose in packages/some-styles/src/brand/host-mochi.ts; its part stays clear.

calls.title: Which NFL celebration is Mochi's (C1530)
options: A touchdown spike, then an end-zone shimmy
An end-zone dance alone, with no ball
A Lambeau leap: a jump out of frame
calls.why: The spike and shimmy read in a long shot and stay inside the box, and arms in a V make the touchdown signal. A leap out of frame would clip in a corner.
calls.undo: Rewrite celebrationAt in packages/some-styles/src/brand/host-mochi.ts; the ceremony's name and its place in the closed set stay.
